Two components per entry: `schema` (a JSON Schema validated with ajv when present) and `forbiddenTopLevel` (a list of keys that must NOT appear at the top of the forwarded args — catches the wrapper-bug class even when we don't have a full per-object schema). Refresh via scripts/capture-inner-schemas.ts when Twenty's server changes.

schema.name: find_people
schema.description: Search for People records using flexible filtering criteria. Supports exact matches, pattern matching, ranges, and null checks. Use limit/offset for pagination and orderBy for sorting. To find by ID, use filter: { id: { eq: "record-id" } }. Returns an array of matching records with their full data.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return (default: 10, max: 100). Start small and increase only if needed.

orderBy.description: Sort records by field(s). CRITICAL for "top N", "largest", "smallest" queries. Each item is an object with exactly ONE property: field name as key, sort direction as value. Example: [{"employees": "DescNullsLast"}] sorts employees descending. Use "DescNullsLast" for top/largest, "AscNullsFirst" for bottom/smallest.

items.description: Object with exactly ONE property: field name as key, OrderByDirection as value. Example: {"employees": "DescNullsLast"}

schema.name: create_view
schema.description: Create a new view for an object. Views define how records are displayed. For KANBAN views, mainGroupByFieldName is required and must be a SELECT field (e.g., "stage", "status"). For CALENDAR views, calendarFieldName and calendarLayout are required.

name.description: View name

objectNameSingular.description: Object name this view is for (e.g., "task", "person", "company")

mainGroupByFieldName.description: Field name to group by (required for KANBAN views, must be a SELECT field, e.g., "stage", "status")

kanbanAggregateOperationFieldName.description: Field name for the kanban aggregate operation (e.g., "amount")

calendarLayout.description: Calendar layout (required for CALENDAR views, e.g., "DAY", "WEEK", "MONTH")

calendarFieldName.description: Date field name to use for the calendar (required for CALENDAR views, must be a DATE or DATE_TIME field, e.g., "createdAt", "dueAt")

fieldNames.description: Field names to display in the view as columns (for TABLE) or cards (for KANBAN/CALENDAR). Fields are displayed in the order provided. Use get_field_metadata to find available field names.

schema.name: update_view
schema.description: Update an existing view. You can change the name and icon.

id.description: View ID to update

name.description: New view name

schema.name: create_view_field
schema.description: Add a new column to a view. View fields define which columns are shown in table or kanban views. First call get_field_metadata to find the fieldMetadataId of the column to add, and get_views to find the target viewId.

viewId.description: The ID of the view to add the field to.

fieldMetadataId.description: The ID of the field metadata to add. Use get_field_metadata to find available fields.

isVisible.description: Whether the field is visible in the view.

position.description: Position of the field in the view (0-based).

schema.name: update_view_field
schema.description: Update properties of a column in a view. You can change its visibility, width (size in pixels), display position, or aggregate operation. Use get_view_fields to find the view field ID. Constraints: position must not be -1, must not precede the label identifier field, and must not conflict with another field's position.

id.description: The ID of the view field to update. Obtain this from get_view_fields.

position.description: Position of the field.

schema.name: create_many_view_fields
schema.description: Add multiple columns to a view at once. More efficient than calling create_view_field multiple times. Each item follows the same schema as create_view_field. All view fields can target the same or different views.

viewFields.description: Array of view fields to create (1-50 items).

viewId.description: The ID of the view to add the field to.

fieldMetadataId.description: The ID of the field metadata to add. Use get_field_metadata to find available fields.

isVisible.description: Whether the field is visible in the view.

position.description: Position of the field in the view (0-based).

schema.name: create_view_filter
schema.description: Add a filter to a view. Use list_object_metadata_items to get fieldMetadataId values.

viewId.description: ID of the view to add the filter to

fieldMetadataId.description: ID of the field to filter on. Use list_object_metadata_items to find field IDs.

operand.description: Filter operator. Valid operators per field type — TEXT/EMAILS/FULL_NAME: CONTAINS, DOES_NOT_CONTAIN, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. NUMBER/NUMERIC: IS, IS_NOT, GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. CURRENCY: GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. DATE/DATE_TIME: IS, IS_RELATIVE, IS_IN_PAST, IS_IN_FUTURE, IS_TODAY, IS_BEFORE, IS_AFTER, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. SELECT: IS, IS_NOT, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. MULTI_SELECT/ARRAY: CONTAINS, DOES_NOT_CONTAIN, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. RELATION: IS, IS_NOT, IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY. BOOLEAN: IS.

value.description: Filter value. Format depends on operand and field type: string for TEXT/SELECT, number for NUMBER/CURRENCY, array of option values for MULTI_SELECT IS/IS_NOT, empty string "" for IS_EMPTY/IS_NOT_EMPTY operators.

subFieldName.description: Required for composite fields — e.g. "amountMicros" for CURRENCY, "addressCity" for ADDRESS, "firstName" or "lastName" for FULL_NAME.

schema.name: update_view_filter
schema.description: Update a filter on a view. Use get_view_filters to find the filter ID.

id.description: ID of the view filter to update

value.description: New filter value

subFieldName.description: New sub-field name for composite fields

schema.name: create_view_sort
schema.description: Add a sort to a view. Use list_object_metadata_items to get fieldMetadataId values.

viewId.description: ID of the view to add the sort to

fieldMetadataId.description: ID of the field to sort by. Use list_object_metadata_items to find field IDs.

create_complete_workflow.$shape: Flat: name, description?, trigger, steps, stepPositions?, edges?, activate?

schema.name: create_complete_workflow
schema.description:
Create a complete workflow with trigger, steps, and connections in a single operation.

CRITICAL SCHEMA REQUIREMENTS:
- Trigger type MUST be one of: DATABASE_EVENT, MANUAL, CRON, WEBHOOK
- NEVER use "RECORD_CREATED" - this is invalid. Use "DATABASE_EVENT" instead.
- Each step MUST include: id (must be a valid UUID), name, type, valid, settings
- CREATE_RECORD actions MUST have objectName and objectRecord in settings.input
- objectRecord must contain actual field values, not just field names
- Use "trigger" as stepId for trigger step in stepPositions and edges

Common mistakes to avoid:
- Using "RECORD_CREATED" instead of "DATABASE_EVENT"
- Missing the "name" and "valid" fields in steps
- Missing the "objectRecord" field in CREATE_RECORD actions
- Using "fieldsToUpdate" instead of "objectRecord" in CREATE_RECORD actions
- Including CODE steps in this tool — this tool does NOT create the underlying logic function needed by CODE steps. Instead, create the workflow without CODE steps first, then add CODE steps individually using create_workflow_version_step (which properly creates the logic function), then call update_logic_function_source to define the code.

IMPORTANT: The tool schema provides comprehensive field descriptions, examples, and validation rules. Always refer to the schema for:
- Field requirements and data types
- Common object patterns and field structures
- Proper relationship field formats
- Variable reference syntax: {{trigger.fieldName}} for trigger data, {{<step-id>.result.fieldName}} for step outputs (step-id is the step's UUID, not its name)
- Error handling options

This is the most efficient way for AI to create workflows as it handles all the complexity in one call.

name.description: The name of the workflow

anyOf.description: Database event trigger that fires when a record is created, updated, deleted, or upserted. The triggered record is accessible in workflow steps via {{trigger.object.fieldName}}.

name.description: Human-readable name for the trigger. Optional but recommended for clarity.

position.description: Position coordinates for the trigger in the workflow diagram. Use (0, 0) for the trigger step.

nextStepIds.description: Array of step IDs that the trigger connects to. These are the first steps in the workflow.

eventName.description: Event name in format: objectName.action (e.g., "company.created", "person.updated", "task.deleted", "company.upserted"). Use lowercase object names.

outputSchema.description: Schema defining the output data structure. For database events, this includes the record that triggered the workflow accessible via {{trigger.object.fieldName}}.

schema.name: activate_workflow_version
schema.description: Activate a workflow version. This makes the workflow version active and available for execution.

workflowVersionId.description: The UUID of the workflow version to activate

schema.name: deactivate_workflow_version
schema.description: Deactivate a workflow version. This makes the workflow version inactive and unavailable for execution.

workflowVersionId.description: The UUID of the workflow version to deactivate

schema.name: create_workflow_version_step
schema.description: Create a new step in a workflow version. This adds a step to the specified workflow version with the given configuration. If parentStepId is not provided, the step will be appended at the end of the workflow.

workflowVersionId.description: The UUID of the workflow version to add the step to

parentStepId.description: Optional ID of the parent step this step should come after (UUID, or "trigger" for the trigger step). If not provided, the step will be added at the end of the workflow.

nextStepId.description: Optional ID of the step this new step should connect to

position.description: Optional position coordinates for the step

defaultSettings.description: Settings for the LOGIC_FUNCTION step. Must include input.logicFunctionId.

logicFunctionId.description: The ID of the logic function. Use list_logic_function_tools to discover available IDs.

workflowVersionId.description: The UUID of the workflow version to add the step to

nextStepId.description: Optional ID of the step this new step should connect to

position.description: Optional position coordinates for the step

defaultSettings.description: Optional default settings for the step.

schema.name: create_workflow_version_edge
schema.description: Create a connection (edge) between two workflow steps. This defines the flow between steps.

workflowVersionId.description: The UUID of the workflow version

source.description: The source step: "trigger" or a step UUID

target.description: The UUID of the target step

sourceConnectionOptions.description: Optional connection options for iterator steps

schema.name: create_draft_from_workflow_version
schema.description: Create a new draft workflow version from an existing one. This allows for iterative workflow development.

workflowVersionIdToCopy.description: The UUID of the workflow version to create a draft from

createNoteTarget.$shape: GraphQL mutation — variables: { data: { noteId, targetCompanyId?, targetPersonId?, targetOpportunityId? } }
createNoteTarget.$comment: Bypasses the record-crud workflow gate by routing through Twenty's GraphQL createOne resolver. The fixture validates the GraphQL `variables` payload, not an execute_tool arguments payload.

schema.name: get_field_metadata
schema.description: Find fields metadata. Retrieve information about the fields of objects in the workspace data model.

id.description: Unique identifier for the field metadata. If provided, returns a single field.

objectMetadataId.description: Filter fields by object metadata ID.

limit.description: Maximum number of fields to return.

schema.name: get_view_filters
schema.description: List all filters applied to a view. Each filter defines a condition that records must match to appear in the view.

viewId.description: ID of the view to list filters for. Obtain this from get_views.

schema.name: get_object_metadata
schema.description: Find objects metadata. Retrieve information about the data model objects in the workspace.

id.description: Unique identifier for the object metadata. If provided, returns a single object.

limit.description: Maximum number of objects to return.
